walkthroughs.body_html:
Human Geography: Population — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Human Geography: Population brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Human Geography: Population.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the replacement fertility rate?

options: Malthus
Boserup
Ehrlich
Rostow

mcqs.q: What happens in Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model?
options: Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Birth rates rise rapidly because people want larger families.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Death rates fall rapidly (due to better food, sanitation and medicine) while birth rates remain high, causing rapid population growth.

mcqs.q: Why is an ageing population a challenge for HICs?
options: Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Because old people stop contributing anything to society.
Rising dependency ratio means fewer workers support more pensioners through tax, increasing pressure on pensions, healthcare and social care services.
Because old people consume too much food.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Because old people consume too much food.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
